Note::TexAccessor::subsubsections¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::TexAccessor::subsubsections() const

Extract Subsubsection Titles Per Source Cell¶

subsubsections() extracts the required brace body from each complete \subsubsection or \subsubsection* command — the third heading level, one below subsections and two below sections. It shares every rule documented on subsections: the optional square-bracket short-title argument is discarded, a nested brace group inside the required body is kept whole, the match is command-exact (a shallower \subsection{...} in the same source is not a \subsubsection and is skipped), and an escaped or unterminated call produces no token.

The closed TokenBatch stores every extracted title in its rank-1 Text tokens() Note. Its Int64 offsets() has source.numel() + 1 entries, so flattened source cell i owns [offsets[i], offsets[i + 1]). The original rank and shape determine lane order but are not imposed on a ragged token count. The receiver is not mutated.

Undefined yields undefined tokens with offsets [0]. Empty cells, malformed commands, and cells without subsubsections produce empty intervals. Only Text is accepted.

Example 1: Optional Argument, Nested Body, And A Shallower Heading¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\subsubsection[Short]{Deep {title}} \subsubsection*{Second})",
    R"(\subsection{shallower} \subsubsection{Third})", "plain"});
const auto deep = source.tex().subsubsections();

std::cout << deep.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["Deep {title}", "Second", "Third"]

The Short value is discarded, {title} is kept whole, and the shallower \subsection{shallower} in cell 1 is not a match — only its trailing \subsubsection{Third} contributes a token.

Example 2: Per-Cell Offsets¶

std::cout << "offsets=[";
const auto offsets = deep.offsets().integers();
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

offsets=[0, 2, 3, 3]

Cell 0 owns two titles, cell 1 owns the one trailing title, and the plain cell 2 owns none.

Example 3: No Subsubsections In Either Cell¶

const auto empty_batch = pluss::make_note({"plain", ""}).tex().subsubsections();
std::cout << empty_batch.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[0], dim=1, numel=0, encoding=utf8)
[]

A source with no matching command anywhere produces a defined, empty flat token Note — not an undefined one; compare Example 4 below.

Example 4: Undefined And Non-Text Input¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().subsubsections().tokens().defined()
          << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2}).tex().subsubsections();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "subsubsections Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
subsubsections Int64: rejected
